text:
anya: hey team — first day here, hi! I can connect to the company VPN but can't ssh to my devbox (10.40.5.12). browser to internal docs 404. VPN status shows CONNECTED. anyone seen this on home/guest wifi?

devon: welcome :) quick Qs — are you on mac/windows/linux? are you using split-tunnel client or full tunnel? can you paste the output of `ip route` (linux/mac) or `route print` (windows)?

anya: macbook m1, macOS Ventura. client says split-tunnel (company vpn). paste below — i redacted some ip addresses:
```
default via 192.168.0.1 dev en0
10.40.0.0/16 via 192.168.0.1 dev en0   <-- ???
172.16.50.0/24 via utun2
```

anya: so traffic to 10.40.x is going to my local gateway, not the tunnel.

devon: yep that explains it. sounds like the client failed to push the internal route, or macOS replaced it because of interface metric. two quick workarounds:
- add a manual route on your laptop (mac): `sudo route -n add -net 10.40.0.0/16 <vpn-gw-ip>`
- or on windows: `netsh interface ip add route 10.40.0.0/16 \"Your VPN Interface\" <vpn-gw-ip> metric=1`

mike: if you're behind some home gateway doing CGNAT or weird DNS, captive portal, etc, tethering to phone mobile hotspot often bypasses the router oddities. also check company SSO/Okta popups — sometimes the VPN session is 'connected' but the SSO cookie isn't set so internal auth fails.

anya: thanks — how do i find the vpn gateway IP to use in the route? `netstat -rn` shows utun2 172.16.50.1 for me. should i use that?

devon: yep use the utun/ppp gateway (172.16.50.1 in your output). try: `sudo route -n add -net 10.40.0.0/16 172.16.50.1` and then `ping 10.40.5.12`. if that works, we can make it persistent.

anya: okay doing that now...

anya: ping works! can ssh now. thanks :-)

anya: small follow-up — will this persist after reboot?

devon: on mac it won't persist by default. we usually push a policy but for quick persistent on mac you can create a small launchd job, or on homebrew-managed systems use /etc/route or `networksetup -setadditionalroutes` depending on version. LMK if you want a snippet.

mike: filed a quick tip in the new-hires checklist about using mobile hotspot as fallback: saves a lot of triage time. :memo:

infra-bot: Created infra ticket TKT-4321: \"vpn route push failure — macOS client occasionally loses internal 10.40/16 route when home gateway present\" assigned to @devon.

anya: awesome, thanks everyone. saved my afternoon :)

okta-bot: Reminder: if you hit SSO during onboarding, open the Okta link in your default browser to complete registration before connecting VPN.
